messages.author: 71171f0d61fc140f
messages.subject: R Markdown & Animation
parts:
I'd like to incorporate an animation into a presentation I'm working on using knitr + R Markdown + pandoc. The default behavior appears to be to convert the figures to mp4, but I actually really prefer the embedded animations from the animation wiki: http://animation.yihui.name/animation:create_html_animation_page but I can't figure out the chunk options, or if there are chunk options to do this.

-Joe

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] R Markdown & Animation
parts:
This is something we were working on in the summer. Examples will be
given soon. Here is a preliminary example:
http://taiyun.github.com/blog/2012/07/k-means/

Basically it is just opts_knit$get(animation.fun = hook_scianimator).
The rest of the job is to get the CSS and JS files into the HTML
document.

Regards,

messages.author: 129e07bdb789652f
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] R Markdown & Animation
parts:
Hello. 

In order to get a scianimator animation in a html generated from a Rmd file I add that :

<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntax.css" type="text/css" />
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/screen.css" type="text/css" media="screen, projection" />
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/scianimator.css" /><br/>
  <script src="/js/jquery-1.4.4.min.js"></script>
  <script src="/js/jquery.scianimator.min.js"></script>

That works but the background of the animation is grey. How to get a white background please ?

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] R Markdown & Animation
parts:
If you are using base graphics, you probably want to set the
background to be white by par(bg = "white")
